claim: In 2026 the road to the Lagos de Covadonga is closed to private traffic during Easter (Mar 28-Apr 12 with some bridges), May weekends, the full Jun 1-Oct 18 stretch, plus Oct 24-25/31 and Nov 1-2; during regulated days only authorised vehicles (reduced mobility, refuge guests) may drive up.
quote: the access road to the Lakes will remain closed to traffic from 00:00 to 24:00 ... Only authorized vehicles—those with reduced mobility documentation or refuge reservations—can access the road.

claim: The 2026 Plan Lagos shuttle costs €9 adult round-trip (valid all day), €3.50 for children 4-11, free under 3, with the Cangas de Onís-Covadonga leg priced separately at €1.55 one-way.
quote: Adults (round-trip, all-day valid): €9 ... Children 4-11 years: €3.50 ... Children under 3: Free ... One-way Cangas de Onís-Covadonga shuttle: €1.55

claim: Shuttle buses run every 30 minutes; April-September the first bus is 8:00 and last ascent 17:45 with final return at 20:50, while October-December 8 the last ascent is 16:00 and final return 19:05; designated park-and-rides are Cangas de Onís bus station (P1, 419 spaces), El Repelao (P4, 142) and El Peregrino (P5, 135), each €2/day.
quote: P1 - Cangas de Onís bus station (419 spaces) ... P4 - El Repelao (142 spaces) ... P5 - El Peregrino (135 spaces) ... All parking costs €2 daily.

claim: The PR-PNPE 2 lakes loop is a low-difficulty 5 km / 2.5 h long route (or 3 km / 1 h short version) starting at the Buferrera car park with only ~50 m of elevation, passing the Príncipe and Entrelagos viewpoints, the Buferrera mines, Lake Ercina and Lake Enol.
quote: Long route: 5 km, 2.5 hours ... Short route: 3 km, 1 hour ... Altitude gain/loss: 50 meters ... Difficulty level: Low

claim: The Covadonga lakes circular route is around 6 km of low difficulty and one of the most accessible in the park, taking in glacial lakes, beech forests, viewpoints and remains of mining activity.
quote: circular route about six kilometres long and of low difficulty that allows you to enjoy glacial lakes, beech forests, spectacular viewpoints and remains of mining activity

claim: The Sanctuary of Covadonga (basilica and Santa Cueva) is open 365 days a year and entry is free, though visitors are asked to respect mass times.
quote: abren todos los días del año de 8 h a 20 h ... se ruega a los visitantes que respeten los horarios de misas y cultos

claim: Entry to the basilica itself is free; a typical schedule is 09:00-13:30 and 15:30-19:00 (extending in peak season), and during busy periods sanctuary parking is regulated with shuttle service replacing direct car access.
quote: La entrada al templo en sí suele ser gratuita como lugar de culto ... 09:00–13:30 y 15:30–19:00 ... se limita el acceso con regulación de tráfico y aparcamiento vigilado

claim: The Bulnes funicular costs €17.61 one-way / €22.16 round-trip for adults and €4.32/€6.71 for children 4-12 in 2026, running every 30 minutes (high season ~10:00-20:00, low season ~10:00-18:00) and covering 2,227 m with a 400 m climb in about 7 minutes.
quote: Adult one-way: €17.61 ... Adult round-trip: €22.16 ... Children (4-12) one-way: €4.32 ... around 7 minutes to traverse 2,227 meters with a 400-meter elevation change

claim: Bulnes splits into Bulnes de Abajo and Bulnes de Arriba (El Castillo) 600 m higher, with the upper village giving the best Texu canal views and the surroundings offering panoramas of the Naranjo de Bulnes (Picu Urriellu, 2,519 m).
quote: Bulnes de Abajo (lower village) and Bulnes de Arriba/El Castillo (upper village) ... 600 meters higher and offers the best views of the Texu Canal

claim: Arriondas to the Lagos de Covadonga is about 29 km by road, roughly 45 minutes' drive — inside the 30 km radius from Casa Marcial, with Covadonga sanctuary at roughly 17 km along the same route.
quote: La distancia entre Arriondas y Lagos de Covadonga es 29 km

claim: Poncebos (base of the Bulnes funicular and Cares gorge trailhead) is about 44 km / 48 minutes from Arriondas — outside the 30 km radius but commonly combined as a longer half-day from the area.
quote: Arriondas to Poncebos by car: The distance is 44 kilometers and the driving time is approximately 48 minutes

claim: The funicular has run since 2001, replacing what had been Spain's last road-less inhabited village; the alternative arrival is the Canal del Texu footpath from Poncebos (about 4 km, ~1h30 walking).
quote: Bulnes gained accessibility since 2001 through the funicular, transforming a previously remote mountain village into a popular tourist destination
